claims: theorem-a/note/main.tex (v0.2, 2026-10-24, 10.5281/zenodo.23624565), Theorem 1 (Theorem A): for every integer k >= 6, w(k) < 4 sqrt(2k) + 2; equivalently c*(k) < 4 sqrt(2k) + 1, so c*(k) <= ceil(sqrt(32k)), and s(n) < k for every integer n <= k^2 - ceil(sqrt(32k)) - 1, where w(k) = k^2 - max{N : s(N) < k} and c*(k) = max{c : s(k^2 - c) = k} = w(k) - 1.

The construction: Ryu's L-shaped packing of side S = k - b + W < k, an aligned (k - b)^2 grid and two bands of b tilted rows at t = tan(theta/2) just above 1/b, with both ends of each band filled by axis-parallel rows (lift 0 at one end, the whole free length at the other) and b the odd integer with |b - sqrt(2k)| <= 1; t is 'close' when the conditions (a)-(d) of Section 4 hold. Lemma 1 (fill), Lemma 2 (band), equation (1) and the proof of Theorem A in Sections 2 to 5.
Remark (sharpness): for odd b >= 5 and k = (b^2 - b + 8)/2 the construction at close t has waste exactly 4b.

Section 6: lband.py decides the bound for 6 <= k <= 60000 and every inequality of the proof for 6 <= k <= 20000, exactly, with least slack B(k) - w = 8019401/78023840599 at k = 19705; a fixed squeeze of 10^-7 fails at k = 43218; strict certificates for 6 <= k <= 40 and k = 101, 300, 600 pass the author's checker and Evan Daniel's; the optimized constructions (waste at most 4 sqrt(2k) + 1.18 for 15 <= k <= 300, 9946 squares below side 100, gains at k = 25, 30, 40) are stated without certificates.

Section 7: comparisons with Daniel's 4 ceil(sqrt(2k - 7)) - 1 (ours smaller at 495210 of 7 <= k < 10^6, his at 255215, tied at 249568), Ryu's Theorems 1.2, 1.3, 1.4 and 1.6, and the author's earlier k - 1 - F(k); 'Theorem A is of the same strength as Daniel's earlier bound, not a new record for any range of k.'

theorem-a/certs/: 36 certificates k006.cert to k040.cert and k101.cert in Evan Daniel's text format, each the closed packing scaled once about the origin by 1 + (k - S)/(2S), side (S + k)/2 < k; SHA256SUMS. LARGE.sha256 states the SHA-256 of the unshipped k = 300 and 600 certificates (89,902 and 359,860 squares), which regenerate.sh rebuilds with lband.py.
